listed_sector_signals.signal: Solar-powered hydrogen production through water electrolysis.
listed_sector_signals.quote:
Solar–hydrogen systems
utilize PV technology to produce electricity from sunlight, which powers an electrolyzer
that splits water into hydrogen and oxygen through electrolysis.

listed_sector_signals.signal: Industrial-scale solar–hydrogen installations appear in the literature review.
listed_sector_signals.quote:
Lately, extensive research (Table 3) has been performed to examine the possibilities
of solar–hydrogen systems in different applications, from small residential systems to big
industrial installations.

listed_sector_signals.signal: Ammonia is mentioned as a hydrogen storage and transportation carrier; ammonia production is not established.
listed_sector_signals.quote:
Large-scale storage and transportation methods have been reviewed, including
compressed and liquid hydrogen, pipeline blending, and ammonia-based carriers.
listed_sector_signals.sector: continuous chemical production (sulfuric acid, ammonia, methanol, fertilizers, chlor-alkali)

listed_sector_signals.signal: A cited PEM electrolyzer model simulates hydrogen flow and is supported by experimental data.
listed_sector_signals.quote:
the model accurately simulates key parameters like current, voltage, and
hydrogen flow through a Data Acquisition System (DAQ). Experimental data confirm the
DR model’s efficacy, making it a valuable asset in modeling PEMEL performance under
varying conditions and advancing efficient hydrogen storage applications [79].

listed_sector_signals.signal: Hydrogen production technologies include solid oxide electrolysis and electrified steam methane reforming in the literature review.
listed_sector_signals.quote:
The review identifies solid
oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) as a leading technology, along with promising alternatives
like anion exchange membranes (AEMs) and electrified steam methane reforming (ESMR).

listed_sector_signals.signal: The methodology describes sensor data from a solar–hydrogen system, including hydrogen storage levels.
listed_sector_signals.quote:
The dataset consists of time-series information gathered from
different sensors integrated into the solar–hydrogen system. The data encompass
key metrics such as energy production and consumption, hydrogen storage levels,
and environmental factors.

independence, ensuring continuous
energy supply without relying on
external sources.

one_line: The paper tests solar-panel image classifiers and proposes ISO 50001 energy management for university solar–hydrogen systems, using Kangwon National University as its organizational example.
